title: Fare Policy (2023 revision)
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Purpose
This policy sets the fares charged on all MRTA bus and light rail services.

2. Standard fares
A single adult fare is $2.75 and is valid for 90 minutes of travel including transfers.
A day pass is $7.00. A 31-day pass is $85.00.

3. Concessions
Riders aged 65 and over, riders under 18, and holders of a valid disability card pay a
reduced fare of $1.25. Proof of eligibility must be carried.

4. Children
Up to two children under the age of 6 travel free when accompanied by a fare-paying adult.

5. Transfers
Transfers are automatic when paying with a stored-value card. Cash fares do not include
a transfer.

title: Refunds and Fare Adjustments
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Scope
This procedure covers refunds of stored-value balances, unused passes, and fares charged
in error.

2. Stored-value balances
A rider may request a refund of a stored-value balance at any staffed station. Balances
under $10.00 are refunded in cash. Balances of $10.00 or more are refunded to the
original payment method within 14 business days.

3. Unused passes
A 31-day pass may be refunded pro rata within the first 7 days of its validity period.
After 7 days no refund is available. Day passes are not refundable once first used.

4. Fares charged in error
Where a rider is charged twice for the same journey, the duplicate charge is reversed
automatically within 3 business days. No application is required. Where an incorrect
fare class was applied, the rider must apply within 60 days.

5. Lost cards
A registered card that is lost may have its balance transferred to a replacement card for
a $5.00 fee. An unregistered card cannot be replaced and its balance is forfeited.

title: Accessibility on MRTA Services
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Commitment
All MRTA vehicles are low-floor and equipped with a ramp or a lift.

2. Priority seating
The first four rows on every bus are priority seating. Riders are asked to give up these
seats to riders with disabilities, older riders, and pregnant riders.

3. Mobility devices
A mobility device up to 30 inches wide and 48 inches long can be accommodated on all
vehicles. Two securement positions are provided on each bus and four on each light rail
vehicle.

4. Service animals
Service animals travel free and are permitted on all vehicles at all times. Operators may
ask two questions only: whether the animal is required because of a disability, and what
work or task it has been trained to perform.

5. Requesting a stop announcement
Automated announcements are made at every stop. A rider may ask the operator to announce
a specific stop.

title: Bicycles, Scooters and Personal Devices
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Bicycles on buses
Every bus carries a front-mounted rack holding two bicycles. Racks are first come, first
served. Riders load and unload their own bicycles. Tandem bicycles and cargo bicycles do
not fit the rack and are not permitted.

2. Bicycles on light rail
Bicycles are permitted on light rail at all times except weekdays between 07:00 and 09:00
and between 16:00 and 18:00. A maximum of two bicycles per vehicle applies.

3. Folding bicycles
A folded bicycle is treated as luggage and may be carried at any time on any service.

4. Electric scooters
Electric scooters and hoverboards using lithium-ion batteries are not permitted on any
MRTA vehicle following the battery fire on route 42 in August 2023.

5. Wheeled luggage
Wheeled luggage is permitted where it does not block an aisle.

title: Governance and Delegated Authority
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. The Board
The Metro Regional Transit Authority (MRTA) is governed by a Board of nine members
appointed by the Regional Transit Governance Council (RTGC). The Board meets monthly.

2. Delegations
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) holds delegated authority for expenditure up to
$250,000. The Chief Operating Officer (COO) holds delegated authority up to $100,000.
Expenditure above $250,000 requires Board approval.

3. Committees
The Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) reviews the annual financial statements. The Service
Planning Committee (SPC) reviews route changes. The Accessibility Advisory Panel (AAP)
advises on compliance with the Regional Accessible Transit Standard (RATS).

4. Reporting
The CEO reports to the Board monthly. The Board reports to the RTGC quarterly. The ARC
reports to the Board twice yearly.

title: Fare Evasion and Enforcement
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Proof of payment
The light rail network operates on proof of payment. A rider must be able to present a
valid fare on request by a Fare Enforcement Officer (FEO).

2. Penalties
A first offence carries a penalty of $75.00. A second offence within 12 months carries a
penalty of $150.00. A third offence within 12 months is referred for prosecution.

3. Appeals
A rider may appeal a penalty within 30 days. Appeals are heard by an officer who was not
involved in the original notice. The outcome is issued within 21 days.

4. Reduced penalty for concession holders
Where a concession holder held a valid concession but did not carry proof, the penalty is
reduced to $15.00 on production of proof within 14 days.

title: Lost Property Procedure
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Where items are held
Items found on MRTA vehicles are transferred to the Lost Property Office at Central
Station within 48 hours.

2. Retention
General items are held for 30 days. Identity documents, bank cards and keys are held for
90 days. Perishable items are disposed of immediately.

3. Claiming
A claimant must describe the item before it is shown to them. Photographic identification
is required. There is no fee.

4. Unclaimed items
Unclaimed items are donated or disposed of after the retention period. Cash is
transferred to the general fund after 90 days.

title: Frequently Asked Questions — Fares
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

How much is a single fare?
An adult single fare is $3.00 and lasts 120 minutes including transfers.

Do children pay?
Two children under 6 travel free with a paying adult. Children aged 6 to 17 pay the
concession fare.

Can I get my money back if I do not use my pass?
A 31-day pass can be refunded pro rata in its first week. See the refunds procedure.

What happens if I am charged twice?
Duplicate charges reverse themselves within three business days. You do not need to do
anything.

Is there a family ticket?
No. MRTA does not offer a family ticket.

text:

Are all buses accessible?

Can I bring my wheelchair?

Can I bring my dog?

Are stops announced?
Yes, automatically at every stop.

title: Service Plan 2026
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Objectives
The 2026 Service Plan sets frequency and coverage targets for the network.

2. Frequency targets
Every route in the core network will operate at a frequency of 10 minutes or better on
weekdays between 06:00 and 20:00 by December 2026. Route 17 and route 42 are the two
remaining routes above this threshold.

3. Coverage
95% of residents in the service area will live within 400 metres of a stop served at
least every 30 minutes.

4. Funding
Delivery is contingent on the operating subsidy approved by the RTGC.

title: Operator Code of Conduct
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Conduct
Operators treat every rider with courtesy regardless of race, religion, disability, or
appearance.

2. Fare disputes
An operator does not refuse travel over a fare dispute. The operator records the incident
and the rider travels. Fare enforcement is not an operator's role.

3. Mobile devices
An operator does not use a mobile device while a vehicle is in motion, including at a
signal.

4. Assistance
An operator deploys the ramp on request without asking the rider to justify the request.

title: Winter Weather Operations
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Snow routes
When snow accumulation exceeds 4 inches, buses operate on designated snow routes. Snow
routes omit stops on grades steeper than 8%.

2. Light rail
Light rail operates in all weather. In freezing rain, service may be reduced to every 20
minutes to allow de-icing trains to run.

3. Notification
Snow route activation is announced by 05:00 on the day it takes effect.

4. Refunds
No refunds are issued for weather-related delays.

title: Stored Value Card Terms
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Purchase
A stored-value card costs $3.00 and may be loaded with between $5.00 and $200.00.

2. Registration
A card may be registered online. Only a registered card is protected against loss.

3. Expiry
A stored value balance does not expire. A card that has not been used for 36 months is
deactivated and the balance may be reclaimed at a staffed station.

4. Autoload
A registered card may be set to load $20.00 automatically when the balance falls below
$5.00.

title: Complaints and Compliments Procedure
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT

1. How to complain
A complaint may be made online, by phone, or in person at a staffed station.

2. Acknowledgement
A complaint is acknowledged within 2 business days and resolved within 15 business days.

3. Escalation
A rider dissatisfied with the outcome may escalate to the Independent Transit Ombudsman
within 60 days of the response.

4. Compliments
Compliments about an operator are recorded on the operator's file and shared with them.

title: Route 42 Battery Fire — Incident Report Summary
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

Incident MRTA-INC-2023-114.

On 19 August 2023 a lithium-ion battery in a personally owned electric scooter ignited on
a route 42 bus near Beltane Street. The vehicle was evacuated. There were no injuries.
The vehicle was destroyed.

Findings: the battery had been modified with a non-manufacturer cell pack. Detection was
not possible by visual inspection.

Recommendation 1: prohibit electric scooters and hoverboards on all vehicles.
Recommendation 2: install signage at all stops.

Both recommendations were accepted and implemented in the 2024 policy revision.

title: Data Protection and Rider Privacy
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. What is collected
A registered stored-value card records the time and location of each tap.

2. Retention
Tap data is retained for 24 months, then aggregated and the identifiable records deleted.

3. Access
A rider may request their own tap history for the past 24 months at no charge.

4. Disclosure
Tap data is disclosed to law enforcement only on production of a warrant.

title: Contractor Safety Requirements
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Site induction
Every contractor working on MRTA property completes a site induction before first entry.

2. Personal protective equipment
High-visibility clothing and safety footwear are required in all track areas.

3. Track access
No contractor enters a track area without a permit issued by the Rail Operations Control
Centre (ROCC).

4. Incidents
Every incident is reported to the ROCC within one hour.

title: Night Service Pilot
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Scope
Routes 17 and 9 will run hourly between 00:30 and 04:30 on Friday and Saturday nights for
a 12-month pilot beginning 1 November 2026.

2. Fares
The standard adult single fare of $3.00 applies. No night surcharge is charged.

3. Evaluation
The pilot will be evaluated on boardings per hour and on operating cost per boarding. A
report goes to the Service Planning Committee in December 2027.

title: Stop Naming Standard
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Principle
A stop is named for the nearest cross street, not for a business.

2. Format
The format is PRIMARY & CROSS, for example HALLORAN & NINTH.

3. Changes
A stop name change requires approval from the Service Planning Committee and 60 days of
notice.

4. Numbering
Stop numbers are four digits. The first two digits are the primary route serving the
stop. Stop 4213 is served primarily by route 42.

title: Vehicle Cleaning Standard
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT

1. Daily
Every vehicle is swept and litter-picked at the end of each service day.

2. Weekly
Every vehicle receives an interior wash including seats, poles and windows.

3. Biohazard
A biohazard incident removes the vehicle from service immediately for specialist cleaning.

4. Exterior
Exterior washing occurs at least twice weekly.

text:

title: Emergency Evacuation of Light Rail Vehicles
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Authority
Only the operator or ROCC may authorise an evacuation.

2. Procedure
Riders are evacuated through the doors at the front of the vehicle where the platform is
accessible, and through the emergency egress at the rear where it is not.

3. Traction power
Traction power is confirmed isolated by ROCC before any evacuation to the track bed.

4. Mobility devices
A rider using a mobility device is evacuated last where it is safe to do so, and first
where the vehicle is on fire.

title: Bus Stop Balancing Programme
text:
METRO REGIONAL TRANSIT AUTHORITY — PUBLIC DOCUMENT
Uncontrolled when printed. Verify against the register before relying on this copy.

1. Purpose
The programme removes stops that are closer than 250 metres to an adjacent stop, to
reduce journey time.

2. Criteria
A stop is a candidate for removal where it is within 250 metres of another stop, has
fewer than 10 boardings per weekday, and is not the nearest stop to a hospital, school or
senior housing.

3. Consultation
Each removal is consulted on for 30 days.

4. Results to date
41 stops removed. Mean route journey time reduced by 4.2%.
